November 20, 2026 | 11:28 am CST
Rockefeller Center Christmas tree arrives in New York, a 76 ft. tall Norway spruce

The tradition of the Rockefeller Center Christmas Tree dates back to 1931, when construction workers building Rockefeller Center erected a small tree decorated with handmade garlands. Photos by Rockefeller Center.

NEW YORK — The 2026 Rockefeller Center Christmas Tree is a 76-foot-tall Norway spruce from West Edmeston, New York. Approximately 75 years old, the donated tree measures 50 feet in diameter and weighs about 11 tons.

The tree's arrival kicks off the holiday season in New York. To celebrate, Meet the Tree Day returns for its second year with festive, family-friendly activities, special photo moments, and the Holiday Workshop presented by Care Bears and FAO Schwarz.
For more than three decades, Rockefeller Center's head gardener Erik Pauzé has played a central role in selecting the annual Tree, searching for the perfect evergreen to take its place on the Plaza.
"What I look for is a tree you’d want in your living room, but on a grander scale,” Pauze says. “It needs to make people smile the second they see it."
The 2026 Rockefeller Center Christmas Tree Lighting Ceremony will take place on Wednesday, December 2, from 7–10 PM.

The Tree will sparkle with more than 50,000 multicolored LED lights strung along approximately five miles of wire. At its peak sits the dazzling Swarovski star, designed by architect Daniel Libeskind in 2018. Weighing approximately 900 pounds, the star features 70 spikes covered in three million crystals.
